about: corpus/teranode/map.json: the module map of #87 (S8), written 2026-10-14. [D] for every mechanism reading; [SRC] for every citation, read with `git show <commit>:<path>` at the two pins below, never a working tree.

One row per rule of S6 or S7: the reference's function, Teranode's service and function, the mechanism (same, different, absent) and the one obligation issue among #88 to #98 that discharges the row. This table is the input of the refinement relation (#88) and of the absence ledger (#96).

tools/teranode_map.py renders spec/teranode-map.md from this file (deterministic; tools/specgen.py writes it with the other spec pages, so the spec leg's byte-identity check covers it) and `tools/teranode_map.py --verify` resolves every citation at the pins (the cite leg runs it; an absent clone is SKIPPED BY NAME, never a pass).
THE ROW KEYS (the keys of record, which the absence ledger (#96) uses; a key outside this list is refused by the generator, except `ledger`, which is #96's and never read by tools/teranode_map.py):
id          kebab-case, stable, unique: the row's name in #88's obligation list and in #96's ledger; a row is renamed only with both pages

layer       S6 (the transaction state machine, docs/DESIGN-S6.md) or S7 (the node beyond the chain: relay, events, observation, persistence, pruning, miner ID, wire formats; cited at the reference's source directly, S7's pages not yet written)
rule        one sentence: the rule as the reference implements it
lean        the Lean definitions that state it, each {name, file} (the file under lean/ declares the name's last component); [] where the spec has no definition yet
reference   {function, cites}: bitcoin-sv at the reference pin; or {absent: true, where, cites} when the reference has no implementation, `cites` then naming where it would be
teranode    {service, function, cites}: Teranode at its pin; or {absent: true, service, where, cites} when Teranode has no implementation, `cites` then naming where it would be
cites       a list of {file, lines: [from, to], anchor}: `anchor` is a text that occurs in the cited lines at the pin (--verify checks it); the list's head is the primary citation

mechanism   same (the same decision procedure over the same inputs, read at the two tags) | different (another structure, stage, trigger or trust root implements the rule) | absent (one side has none; then exactly one of reference, teranode carries absent: true)

obligation  one issue among #88 to #98: #88 the relation itself, #89 subtree merkle, #90 spend order and conflicts, #91 the sentinel height and the flag word, #92 record lifetimes, #93 chain selection and reorg, #94 the alert system, #95 the per-release divergence report (the rows read as same), #96 the absence ledger (every absent row), #97 the observation contract, #98 the legacy bridge
note        one line: the mechanism difference, or what makes the reading same; a file:line in it is one of the row's cites (the generator refuses it otherwise)
ledger      reserved for #96 (its direction-independent ruling fields); absent in every row this lane wrote

rows.rule: Receive a transaction: the reference's checks in order, ending in accepted, held non-final, orphan or rejected (DESIGN-S6 section 2.1).
rows.note: No pool entry: an accepted transaction is a spend and a create in the UTXO store plus a hand-off to block assembly, so the outcome is a record with its marks, never a membership in a pool.

rows.rule: The context-free transaction gate: structure, sizes, values and the coinbase refusal (CheckRegularTransaction).
rows.note: A port of the same checks into Go; the coinbase refusal is ordered before finality as the reference orders it (Validator.go:902-904).

rows.rule: The per-input script verdict on both paths (the spec's ScriptOracle call sites, DESIGN-S6 section 4.3).
rows.note: Teranode delegates the verdict to GoBDK, a build of the reference's own script source (docs/PROVENANCE.md section 1a); the error mapping is ScriptVerifierGoBDK.go:351 mapBDKValidationError.

rows.rule: Script word selection: the block word from the era of the tip's successor and the per-input contribution from the coin's era.
rows.note: Teranode passes heights, not a word: an unconfirmed parent's sentinel height is replaced at the call boundary and GoBDK derives the flags from the heights.

rows.rule: Spend the inputs: every input exists and is unspent, the values and the fee hold, the coins are spent and the outputs created.
rows.note: One atomic spend per output inside the store, which records the spending data on the spent output; the reference spends in a coins view and flushes it.

rows.rule: A coinbase output is spendable only COINBASE_MATURITY (100) blocks after its block.
rows.note: The maturity height is stored on the coinbase's record and compared inside the store's spend, not computed from the coin's height at validation.

rows.rule: Two transactions spending one outpoint: the accepted spender is kept and the competitor refused (txn-mempool-conflict).
rows.note: The store's atomic spend decides which spender wins; a losing spender can be stored with the conflicting mark rather than refused and forgotten.

rows.rule: Absolute finality: nLockTime against the height and the median time past (IsFinalTx).
rows.note: The same predicate and comparison time; what follows a non-final verdict differs and is the row non-final-hold.

rows.rule: A non-final transaction is held in the non-final pool until it finalises or is replaced (policy, DESIGN-S6 section 2.1 row 3).

teranode.where: the finality check returns ErrNonFinal and nothing is held

rows.note: Teranode refuses a non-final transaction; the reference's hold, its replacement rule and its periodic re-check have no counterpart.

rows.rule: BIP68 relative locks against the coins' heights and median times (a no-op after Genesis).
rows.note: A port of the same lock computation over the parents' heights and median times.

rows.rule: A transaction with a missing parent is held as an orphan and re-evaluated when the parent arrives (policy).
rows.note: Only the legacy P2P path keeps orphans; the propagation surfaces and the Kafka intake keep nothing for a missing parent.

rows.rule: A peer's rejected transaction is remembered in the recent-rejects filter and not re-validated (policy).
rows.note: A bounded map on the legacy path only (maxRejectedTxns 10,000, manager.go:96), cleared wholesale; no filter on the propagation path.

rows.rule: The pool's minimum fee: the configured floor and the rolling minimum raised by eviction (policy).

teranode.function: the MinMiningTxFee policy handed to the engine

rows.note: A fixed fee rate checked inside the engine; no rolling minimum, since nothing is evicted to raise one.

rows.rule: An unconfirmed transaction's lifetime: expiry after -mempoolexpiry with its descendants (policy).
rows.note: Age counted in blocks from unminedSince, not in seconds from entry; an old unmined record is kept and its parents preserved from deletion.

rows.rule: The pool's size bound: TrimToSize evicts the least worthy with descendants until under -maxmempool (policy).

teranode.where: the assembler refuses a batch for room and evicts nothing

rows.note: No eviction by fee rate and no size-driven removal of an accepted transaction.

rows.rule: The block: a header and a flat, ordered list of transactions, the coinbase at its head.
rows.note: The body is a list of subtree hashes, each subtree a list of transaction ids stored apart; the transaction order is the subtrees' concatenation.

rows.rule: The staged path to in-block: transactions grouped into subtrees, validated and announced before the block.

reference.where: the body is the flat transaction list of CBlock; nothing is staged before the block

rows.note: New behaviour the reference never had; the root over subtree roots is the row merkle-root.

rows.rule: The merkle root over the block's transactions, with the mutation flag (bad-txnmrklroot, bad-txns-duplicate).
rows.note: Computed over subtree roots, the coinbase substituted in the head subtree; equality with the flat root for every count and size is #89's theorem.

rows.rule: The block's context-free checks: the merkle root, the coinbase, the size, the per-transaction gate and the sigop sums (CheckBlock).
rows.note: The per-transaction checks ran when each transaction was validated into a subtree; the block pass checks the subtrees, the order and the coinbase.

rows.rule: Connect a block: inputs present and unspent, the scripts under the block word, the coinbase bound, the undo written (ConnectBlock).
rows.note: No undo record: the spends already happened at transaction validation, and connecting marks the records mined (setTxMinedStatus, BlockValidation.go:1410).

rows.rule: Proof of work: the target in range and at most powLimit, the hash at most the target.
rows.note: The same comparison of the header hash with the compact target.

rows.rule: The next work required: the genesis case, no retargeting, the EDA, then the DAA from daaHeight.
rows.note: A port of the same schedule; the historical path is Difficulty.go:181 calcHistoricalWorkRequired.

rows.rule: The header's contextual checks: nBits equal to the work required, the time above the median time past and at most two hours ahead, the version floors.
rows.note: The same checks; the wall-time bound reads the node's clock on both sides.

rows.rule: The median time past of the last eleven headers.
rows.note: The same median, served by height from the blockchain store.

rows.rule: BIP34: from BIP34Height the coinbase begins with the serialized block height (bad-cb-height).
rows.note: The same activation height and push; Teranode reads the block's height from the push.

rows.rule: The coinbase pays at most the subsidy plus the fees (bad-cb-amount).
rows.note: The same bound; the fees come from the stored records rather than a coins view.

rows.rule: The block's serialized size against GetMaxBlockSize (-excessiveblocksize; C/setting in DESIGN-S6 section 2.2).
rows.note: Teranode declines an oversize block as a local policy (ErrBlockPolicyDeclined) and never marks its hash invalid; the reference refuses it with bad-blk-length.

rows.rule: The transaction order in a block: a parent before its child (TTOR, a local policy in the source's words).
rows.note: Checked with each transaction's blessed state on every block except the checkpoint fast path (model/Block.go:1099); the reference checks blocks MIN_TTOR_VALIDATION_DISTANCE (100) or more from the tip (validation.cpp:5671-5672).

rows.rule: BIP30: a transaction may not overwrite an unspent output of the same id (the two historic exceptions, the BIP34 shortcut).
rows.note: A record keyed by the transaction id cannot be created twice; the reference tests the outputs of the id in the coins view.

rows.rule: A header at a checkpointed height must carry the checkpoint's hash (a setting).
rows.note: The same test against the chain parameters' checkpoint list.

rows.rule: Assumed-valid: script checks skipped below the configured block when the best header has enough work (a setting).

teranode.function: the OutpointOnlySpend path at or below the highest checkpoint

rows.note: Teranode skips scripts for a header-proven block below the highest checkpoint on the legacy path with no setting (quickValidationAllowed, handle_block.go:655-665; WithSkipScriptValidation, handle_block.go:1461); only the outpoint-only spend is a setting, off by default (settings.go:411); neither is an assumed-valid hash and a work floor.

rows.rule: The active chain is the most-work valid candidate; equal work orders by completion time, then sequence id.
rows.note: A query over stored blocks not marked invalid, equal work ordered by peer id and then insertion id; the reference orders equal work by completion time, then sequence id.

rows.rule: Reorganize: disconnect to the fork, connect forward, re-admit the disconnected transactions and remove what no longer holds.
rows.note: No undo: the records stay and their longest-chain marks flip while the assembler moves its subtrees back and forward; a reorg of at least CoinbaseMaturity blocks resets the assembler and re-checks the unmined inputs (BlockAssembler.go:2225-2231).

rows.rule: The operator's hands on the candidate set: invalidateblock marks a block failed and re-activates; reconsiderblock clears the marks.
rows.note: A stored invalid flag set on the block and every descendant in one statement (stores/blockchain/sql/InvalidateBlock.go:42-44); the alert service can also invalidate (services/alert/node.go:160).

rows.rule: The soft consensus freeze: a block spending a consensus-frozen output is held from selection for a configured number of blocks (a setting).

teranode.where: the best header query selects among blocks not marked invalid; no freeze state exists

rows.note: No soft rejection and no frozen-block hold in Teranode's selection.

rows.rule: Safe mode: a large valid fork warns the client and restricts RPC, with no effect on validity.

teranode.where: the chain tips are reported; no fork level is derived from them

rows.note: A client behaviour of the reference with no counterpart; validity is unaffected on both sides.

rows.rule: The node's own state machine: IDLE, RUNNING and CATCHINGBLOCKS, gating relay and assembly.

reference.where: the closest state is the initial-block-download latch; no explicit machine

rows.note: New behaviour: relay is suppressed outside RUNNING (services/legacy/peer_server.go:2149).

rows.rule: Frozen outputs and confiscation transactions: the operator's lists checked on both paths (a third kind, neither consensus nor policy alone; #70).

teranode.function: Node.AddToConsensusBlacklist; Node.AddToConfiscationTransactionWhitelist; the store's freeze and reassign

rows.note: The same lists arrive through the alert system's messages instead of the operator's RPC, and a confiscation reassigns the output in the store.

rows.rule: The alert system: signed network messages that freeze, confiscate, invalidate and ban.

reference.where: the operator's RPC is the reference's only route to the lists

rows.note: A different trust root for the same parameters (#94 records it); absent from the reference's tree at the pin.

rows.rule: The block template: the journal's transactions in order, served as a mining candidate.
rows.note: A candidate over completed subtrees from the subtree processor; the reference's comes from its journal.

rows.rule: Transaction relay: a peer's tx message validated, then announced to the other peers by inventory.
rows.note: The reference's wire protocol is spoken only by the legacy bridge; Teranode's own intake is the propagation service (gRPC, HTTP, Kafka).

rows.rule: Compact block relay: a header and short transaction ids, reconstructed from the pool.

teranode.where: the legacy bridge takes whole blocks

rows.note: No compact block message in the legacy bridge at the tag.

rows.rule: Double-spend notification: a detected double spend reported to the registered endpoints and peers (dsdetected).

teranode.where: the conflict is recorded as a mark and nothing is sent

rows.note: No dsdetected or double-spend notification code in Teranode's Go files at the tag.

rows.rule: The node's event surface: what a subscriber hears about transactions and blocks.
rows.note: Disjoint vocabularies: ZMQ topics on one side, Kafka topics and the blockchain service's notifications on the other; the two absences are the next rows.

rows.rule: ZMQ publication of transactions and blocks.

teranode.where: the Kafka topics stand where a ZMQ publisher would

rows.note: No ZMQ publisher in Teranode's Go files at the tag.

rows.rule: Kafka topics for transactions, metadata, subtrees, blocks and rejections.

reference.where: the ZMQ interface stands where a Kafka producer would

rows.note: New behaviour the reference never had.

rows.rule: The observation surface: the RPC an outside party reads a transaction's and a block's state through (DESIGN-S6 section 3's observables).
rows.note: getrawmempool answers from the block assembler's transactions, not from a pool; the asset service adds an HTTP surface the reference does not have.

rows.rule: The merkle proof surface: a transaction's path to its block's root (getmerkleproof2, TSC format; #75).
rows.note: Served over the asset HTTP from subtree data; the reference serves it over RPC from the block file.

rows.rule: The pool across a restart: dumped to disk at shutdown and loaded at start.
rows.note: Nothing is dumped: the unmined records live in the persistent UTXO store and the assembler reloads them by iteration.

rows.rule: Block storage: each connected block written to the block files with its undo data.
rows.note: A separate service writes the block, its subtree data and a per-block UTXO difference set after validation (persist_block.go:20-33); the reference writes the block and its undo record in the connection.

rows.rule: Pruning: block files removed below a retained depth (-prune).
rows.note: UTXO records carry a deletion height (deleteAtHeight, overridden by preserveUntil) and the pruner removes them by height; the reference prunes whole block files.

rows.rule: Miner ID: the coinbase document, its key rotation and revocation, and the authenticated connection.

teranode.where: the authch handshake is answered with no Miner ID

rows.note: One Go file names Miner ID at the tag, to say it is not supported.

rows.rule: The transaction wire format: version, inputs, outputs, lock time.
rows.note: Inside Teranode a transaction travels extended with each input's previous satoshis and locking script; the legacy bridge speaks the reference's format.

rows.rule: The block wire format: the header, the transaction count and every transaction.
rows.note: Teranode's block bytes carry the subtree hashes and the coinbase, not the transactions; the legacy bridge serves the reference's format.
